text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"Polymorphism in Java means one name or interface can take different behaviors depending on context.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c2","text":"Compile-time polymorphism in Java is method overloading, where the compiler picks a method by its parameter list before the program runs.","cited_pids":["5974f259d0f5#0","5160a72f8912#2"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"Runtime polymorphism in Java is method overriding, where the JVM picks the version belonging to the actual object.","cited_pids":["5974f259d0f5#0","c5005aa3ff83#0"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"Runtime polymorphism is achieved through dynamic method dispatch.","cited_pids":["5974f259d0f5#0","c5005aa3ff83#0"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"Some sources argue that overloading is a naming convenience resolved statically rather than true polymorphism.","cited_pids":["667aeb21156d#2"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"A Medium article argues that true polymorphism exists only through overriding, not overloading.","cited_pids":["29552994a8fa#0"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"GeeksforGeeks counts method overloading as a form of polymorphism.","cited_pids":["5160a72f8912#0"]}]}
